commentary_faqs.question: Practice: Ghatastha Yoga (Purification/Shatkarma preparation)
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Ghatastha Yoga, where the human body is viewed as a clay pot (ghata) that must be baked and purified in the fire of yoga before spiritual advancement is possible. It also emphasizes the traditional system of acquiring knowledge by approaching a Guru with humility (vinaya) and devotion (bhakti).

commentary_faqs.question: Therapeutic & Somatic Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: The purification of the physical body (vessel/ghata) through Shatkarmas acts as a detoxification protocol. In modern yoga therapy, this forms the foundation for managing metabolic, respiratory, and psychosomatic disorders by clearing systemic blockages and rebalancing the autonomic nervous system.

sanskrit_shloka: न जायते वार्द्धकं च ज्वरो नैव प्रजायते । भवेत्स्वच्छन्ददेहश्च कफदोषं निवारयेत् ॥
text: न जायते वार्द्धकं च ज्वरो नैव प्रजायते । भवेत्स्वच्छन्ददेहश्च कफदोषं निवारयेत् ॥
transliteration: na jāyate vārddhakaṃ ca jvaro naiva prajāyate | bhavetsvacchandadehaśca kaphadoṣaṃ nivārayet ||
translation: Old age does not arise, nor does fever occur; the body becomes free and self-determined, and the phlegm-based humor (kapha) is pacified.
